chapter_title: AI Agents, Prompts, and Rubric Scoring
learning_objective: The learner will identify the seven parts of a prompt from a description of how each looks, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** prompt-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the seven parts of a prompt from a description of how each looks, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Prompt, AI Assistant, Large Language Model (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A prompt is only a question. (2) The example is optional decoration. (3) A placeholder is part of the final text the model sees. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying the parts of a prompt is a Remember-level task, and an illustration of one prompt as a page of stacked blocks gives each part a place. The quiz asks the learner to recognize a part by its look. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of a prompt as a page of stacked blocks, each with a small icon at its left. The first block has a person icon and one thin line. The second has a checkbox icon and two thin lines. The third has a document icon and a block of many thin lines with a small bar in braces in the middle. The fourth has a list icon and four short lines. The fifth has a table icon and a small grid. The sixth has a pair of arrows icon and two lines with an arrow between them. The seven markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Role | The first block, with a person icon and one thin line. | Says who the model should act as. | A role sets tone and care, and does not give the model expertise it lacks. | | 2 | Task | The second block, with a checkbox icon and two thin lines. | Says what to do, as a specific action. | Name the action and the criteria. | | 3 | Input | The third block, with a document icon and many thin lines. | The material to work on, like the resource's text. | Paste the source, and do not assume the model knows it. | | 4 | Placeholder | The small bar in braces inside the third block. | A slot that is filled with the real text when the prompt runs. | A placeholder lets one prompt be reused for many resources. | | 5 | Rules | The fourth block, with a list icon and four short lines. | What to do and not do, including what to do when unsure. | Tell the model to write "not checkable" when it cannot tell. | | 6 | Output format | The fifth block, with a table icon and a small grid. | The shape of the answer, like the columns of a table. | A fixed format makes answers easy to compare. | | 7 | Example | The sixth block, with a pair of arrows icon and two lines joined by an arrow. | A sample input and a good answer to it. | One good example shows the format better than a paragraph about it. | **Provenance:** The seven parts follow the chapter section "Prompt". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the prompt "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 7 in the order of the table. Marker 4 sits inside the block of marker 3. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 7 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 7 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 7 correct on the first attempt". At 6 or more it adds "You can read a prompt's parts." Below 6 it lists the labels of the missed parts. **Starting State:** The illustration with seven numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see what it is." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a good prompt has up to six parts: role, task, input, rules, output format, and example. The sim adds the placeholder inside the input block.
